solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Liking early appearance of public transport (8)

indicators.note: the first thing to show of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to transport someone is to delight or enchant them

annotation.surface: Someone is fond of seeing the first bus of the morning turn up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Public transport' reads as one phrase meaning buses and trains; the split falls between the words, and 'transport' is a verb meaning to carry away with delight.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, borrowed from French, for a taste or leaning towards something.

entries.clue: Choice of English lesson delivered in church (8)

blocks.note: a lection is a passage of scripture read aloud at a service

annotation.surface: An English lesson given as a sermon.
annotation.walkthrough: LECTION is an uncommon word, related to lectern and lecture; 'delivered in church' is part of its definition, not an extra instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An election is a choice, as in 'the election of a leader' or 'of his own election'.

entries.clue: Two characters changing positions in discussion for environmental protection (12)

indicators.note: two letters swap places with each other

blocks.note: the V and the S trade places

annotation.surface: A debate about the environment in which two participants swap seats.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'two characters' sound like people in a debate; they are letters, V and S, and swapping them turns talk into protection.
annotation.definitionFit: The everyday green sense: saving habitats, species and resources from damage.

entries.clue: Plying oar, gaunt fellow aboard boat (8)

indicators.note: plying means working busily, so the letters are worked into a new order

annotation.surface: A thin crewman rows away on a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The Argonauts were Jason's crew aboard the Argo in Greek myth, so the modest definition hides a famous ship.
annotation.definitionFit: An Argonaut was one of the men who sailed aboard the Argo with Jason.

entries.clue: Time county’s united to quash one outburst of rage (7)

indicators.note: U squashes and replaces the I, taking its place

blocks.note: Antrim is a county of Northern Ireland

annotation.surface: A county's united front stifles someone's angry outburst.
annotation.walkthrough: ANTRIM is a county in Northern Ireland; U for united and I for one are standard abbreviations.
annotation.definitionFit: A tantrum is a sudden outburst of bad temper.

entries.clue: These enable one to track small amounts of money (6)

blocks.note: cents are small sums of money

annotation.surface: Something lets you keep track of every penny you spend.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about budgeting; the definition is about hounds following a trail, where scents are what they track.
annotation.definitionFit: Scents are the smells that let a tracker or dog follow a trail.

entries.clue: Back from hospital, a way to survive (4)

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: A patient home from hospital learns how to pull through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back from hospital' reads as discharge after treatment; it only takes the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that holds out, as in 'it won't make it through winter', does the job.

entries.clue: Anxious condition of Neil’s regularly about money (8)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals, here the 1st, 3rd and 5th
the outer letters go round the money

annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-S counts as a letter here: taking every other letter of NEIL'S keeps the S. The surface reads as Neil worrying about money, which is the answer's own sense.
annotation.surface: Neil keeps worrying about money.
annotation.definitionFit: The psychiatric term for a mental disorder whose chief symptom is persistent worry.

entries.clue: Honour officer stabbing a rebel (8)

indicators.note: a stab goes into something, so the officer goes inside

blocks.note: A + CADE: Jack Cade led a rebellion in 1450

annotation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led the Kent rebellion of 1450 and is a crossword regular; the colonel goes in after A C.
annotation.surface: An officer is decorated for stabbing a rebel.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: originally the touch of a sword conferring knighthood, now any award or praise.

entries.clue: Empty-sounding vessel (4)

indicators.note: tells you the word is heard, not seen

annotation.surface: A hollow pot that rings when struck.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a pot or jar; the vessel is a blood vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one kind of blood vessel, the kind carrying blood back to the heart.

entries.clue: Photographing famous actor — one with brilliant short career? (8,4)

blocks.note: to shoot a scene is to photograph it
a star is a famous actor

annotation.surface: A paparazzo snaps a celebrity whose fame will not last.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition describes a meteor as if it were a celebrity: bright, and gone quickly. The question mark flags that playfulness.
annotation.definitionFit: A shooting star blazes briefly across the sky, a brilliant but short 'career'.

entries.clue: Entering beach, choose vessel, extremely neat (5-3-4)

indicators.note: the choice goes into the beach

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

annotation.surface: Someone heads onto the beach and picks out a very tidy boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The word breaks are misleading: PICK in SANDS gives SPICKANDS, and PAN finishes the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Spick-and-span means very neat and clean.

entries.clue: Some incentive originally to slip a chain (6)

indicators.note: take each word at its origin, its first letter

blocks.note: to err is to slip up

annotation.surface: A dog or prisoner gets encouragement to break free of a chain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chain' sounds like a shackle; it is a chain of mountains.
annotation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged chain of mountains.

entries.clue: Positive moods, with written approvals to move home (2,6)

blocks.note: ups, as in ups and downs
a tick on paper marks approval

annotation.surface: Cheerful people with signed permission to relocate.
annotation.walkthrough: To up sticks is British slang for packing up and moving house; the break UPS + TICKS falls in the middle of STICKS.
annotation.definitionFit: To up sticks is to leave home and move somewhere else.

entries.clue: Find how any other planet may jocularly be defined? (7)

definitions.text: how any other planet may jocularly be defined?

blocks.note: find as in dig up or discover

blocks.clueFragment: how any other planet may jocularly be defined?
blocks.note: every planet but ours is, jokingly, 'not Earth'

annotation.surface: A mock dictionary entry for every planet except ours.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half treats UNEARTH as UN + EARTH, 'not Earth', which fits every other planet; 'jocularly' admits the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: To unearth something is to dig it up or discover it.

entries.clue: Part of shoe damaged — blow! (8)

blocks.note: the upper is the top part of a shoe

annotation.surface: Someone discovers their shoe is ruined and swears.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blow!' reads as a mild curse; it is a punch.
annotation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a punch thrown upward.

entries.clue: Hinder half of solution for long-contested region (7)

indicators.note: take the first three of the six letters

blocks.note: to balk is to hinder or thwart

annotation.surface: Blocking half of a peace plan for a disputed territory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solution' first gives ANSWER and then only half of it is used.
annotation.definitionFit: The Balkans in south-east Europe have been fought over for centuries.

entries.clue: One cat’s run off: she may be up your tree (8)

definitions.text: she may be up your tree

indicators.note: off = gone bad or out of order

annotation.surface: A cat has bolted and may be stuck up your tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The tree sounds like where a runaway cat ends up; it is a family tree, and 'she' is a grandmother or great-aunt.
annotation.definitionFit: An ancestor appears higher up in your family tree.

entries.clue: Self-regarding individual wants borders of scarlet flowers (8)

indicators.note: wants = lacks, so letters are removed

blocks.note: a narcissist is obsessed with themself
outer letters of 'scarlet'; these are removed

annotation.surface: A vain person wants a bouquet edged in red.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wants' reads as desire; here it means lacks. The S and T come off the end of NARCISSIST.
annotation.definitionFit: Narcissi are daffodil-like flowers; the plural of narcissus.

entries.clue: Briefly comment on suspicious page in such a contract (2-5)

indicators.note: cut short, losing the last letter

blocks.note: NOTE, a comment, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone scribbles a note beside a dodgy clause in a contract.
annotation.walkthrough: The contract is a bridge contract, not a legal one: a no-trump bid means no suit is trumps. 'Such a' points back at the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: In bridge, a no-trump contract is played without a trump suit.

entries.clue: Sanctimonious manner towards vegetable (8)

blocks.note: pi is British slang for pious

annotation.surface: A holier-than-thou attitude to vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: PI is a short slang form of 'pious' found in British dictionaries.
annotation.definitionFit: A pimiento is a sweet red pepper.

entries.clue: New university that is switching around parts of atoms (6)

annotation.surface: A newly founded university overhauls its physics department.
annotation.walkthrough: 'University' is usually U; here it is UCL, University College London.
annotation.definitionFit: The physics sense: the dense cores of protons and neutrons at the centre of atoms, in the plural.

entries.clue: Singer, valued informant of mine (6)

blocks.note: caged canaries warned miners of gas

annotation.surface: A vocalist doubles as a prized police informer.
annotation.walkthrough: Singer and informant both suggest a grass; 'of mine' reads as possessive but means a coal mine, where canaries warned of gas.
annotation.definitionFit: A canary is a songbird, and was kept in mines to warn of poisonous gas.

entries.clue: Cross heroine worked out horny types (12)

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An angry heroine figures out who the randy characters are.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Horny' tempts a racier reading; it means having horns.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: 'horny' in its literal sense of horn-bearing, and these animals carry one or two on the snout.

entries.clue: Given that, doubts nothing (2,2)

blocks.note: doubts or conditions, as in 'no ___ or buts'

annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits the clue neatly: the phrase before it is the definition, and the rest reads as a follow-on remark.
annotation.surface: If that is so, there is nothing left to question.
annotation.definitionFit: 'If so' means given that that is the case.

entries.clue: Make available online job (4)

blocks.note: publish on a website or social media

annotation.surface: Advertise a vacancy on the internet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction, advertise a job online; it splits into two senses of the same short word, one a verb and one a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the verb for publishing online, and the noun for an appointment, as in 'a teaching ___'.

entries.clue: Lift very hot water, holding right away from mouth (8)

indicators.note: the steam holds the R inside it

blocks.note: to up = to lift or raise
steam is water heated past boiling

annotation.surface: A dentist raises scalding water to a patient's lips, keeping it clear of the mouth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' is the mouth of a river, where it meets the sea; heading upstream takes you away from it.
annotation.definitionFit: Upstream means towards a river's source, away from its mouth.

entries.clue: Soldier without dog tag perhaps showing fear of persecution (8)

blocks.note: a dog tag is a soldier's identification, ID

annotation.surface: A soldier who has lost his dog tags fears he is being targeted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like an instruction to put letters outside; it simply gives NO, so the pieces sit side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: To be paranoid is to fear, often irrationally, that others are persecuting you.
